newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady on fresh fund injection.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady on fresh fund injection.

text.p: The interbank rates were mostly steady as big banks continued to lend one-month money, dealers said on Monday.
They said the banks were lending on behalf of the central Bank Negara Malaysia, which has been making efforts to keep interest rates down in the face of a sharply falling ringgit.
Bank Negara does not usually comment on its open market operations.
"Rates are around Friday levels. Big banks are still lending one-month," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
"I think authorities are very insistent to keep rates down," said the dealer.
At 0330 GMT, one-month money was at 7.30/40 percent, three-month money was at 7.40/50 percent from 7.40/50 percent and one-week rate was at 6.0 percent, all unchanged from Friday.

Bank Negara is said to be over the past month focusing on keeping interest rates under check after an abandoned defense of the ringgit through intervention drained six to eight billion ringgit from the system.
It also imposed restrictions on local banks to limit their swap transactions to $2.0 million per overseas customer.

Dealers said this has brought many overseas investors to the market to unload their holdings of Malaysian bonds. "There are a lot of offers for bonds from overseas, but not enough demand," one bonds dealer said.
Interest rate futures were hardly traded in the morning session on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange to reflect the uncertainty over the direction of interbank rates.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down one point to 92.48, or an implied yield of 7.52 percent.
